title: Huge crowd gathers to watch local ritual and you'd never guess what it's about - NewsBreak
text: A Minneapolis woman has captured the hearts of the internet by showcasing a quirky local tradition that draws crowds by the hundreds each year, leaving viewers utterly charmed. Jessy Muller, known as ' slowroamer ' to her impressive 256,000 Instagram followers, typically shares snippets of everyday life in Minneapolis. But it's her latest post that's turning heads: a unique celebration involving the sharpening of a giant pencil. She teases her audience at the start of the video, inviting them to "Come with me to see a giant pencil be sharpened". She then revealed the back story, adding: "A guy had a damaged oak tree in his front yard - and then in 2022 he decided to hire a chainsaw sculptor to carve it into a 16ft pencil". READ MORE: Liam Neeson fans raving over Amazon Prime thriller - but critics don't agree READ MORE: Ivanka Trump steals show in white sundress with family at Mets game The artist behind this towering graphite wonder is Curtis Ingvoldstad , who proclaims on his website: "An adventure that I could not resist led me on a path riddled with danger, passion and curiosity. My work is perpetuated by fun, inspiration and a belief in the human spirit." Local weather erodes the tip of the pencil - so to keep it pointy, homeowners John and Amy Higgins host an annual 'sharpening of the pencil' event, complete with "T-shirt cannonballs, music, dancing and pure silliness". The event attracts hundreds of revellers, some donning oversized pencil hats or costumes. Chatting with The Independent , John Higgins detailed: "We tell a story about the dull tip, and we're gonna get sharp. There's a renewal. We can write a new love letter, a thank you note. We can write a math problem, a to-do list. And that chance for renewal, that promise, people really seem to buy into and understand." The 'sharpening' event is truly fascinating; an immense scaffold is built around the tree, complete with an outsized, specially designed red pencil sharpener that a committed group of 'pencil sharpener hoisters'. Using a pulley system, they heave up towards the 'tip' of the 'pencil'. During the 'sharpening', a helper playfully tosses 'pencil shavings' to the enthusiastic onlookers. The quirky spectacle has received 27,000 likes and counting on social media. People have also taken the time to leave positive comments. A viewer ecstatically posted: "The throwing of the faux pencil shavings top tier entertainment. I love weird/quirky/artsy things like this! !" while another commenter declared, "This is the only corner of humanity I want to be involved in". Someone else revealed: "This is the silliest but most wholesome thing on the gram right now", and yet another added affectionately, "Almost forgot: THIS is the *point* I'm movin' to Minneapolis!". The community and its proud pencil proprietors know well that the pencil won't endure indefinitely due to the annual sharpening - but therein lies the enchantment of the tradition – savoring the present moment.
